title: Kingdom of Loango founded
description: A ruler remembered as Njimbe unites the small coastal polities north of the Congo mouth into a kingdom that trades copper, cloth and later slaves with the world.

title: De Brazza's treaty with the Makoko
description: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signs a protectorate treaty with King Iloo I of the Bateke, racing Stanley's advance and planting the flag that grows into Brazzaville.

title: French Congo established
description: The protectorate becomes a formal colony, later leased out to concession companies whose ivory and rubber quotas brutalise whole districts.

title: Renamed Middle Congo
description: The shrunken colony takes the name Moyen-Congo after Gabon and Ubangi-Shari are drawn off.

title: French Equatorial Africa created
description: Gabon, Middle Congo, Ubangi-Shari and Chad are federated as French Equatorial Africa, ruled from Brazzaville until 1958.

title: Congo–Ocean Railway built
description: Forced and recruited labour drives 510 kilometres of line over the Mayombé mountains at the cost of some 17,000 African lives.

title: Capital of Free French Africa
description: After the colonies rally to de Gaulle, Brazzaville becomes the seat of his African administration and briefly of the Paris-recognised Empire Defence Council.

title: Brazzaville Conference
description: De Gaulle's governors meet to plan the post-war empire, promising reform, ending forced labour and ruling out independence.

title: Autonomous republic
description: After voting for de Gaulle's Community the Middle Congo becomes the Republic of Congo with Fulbert Youlou as premier.

title: Independence from France
description: The Republic of the Congo becomes fully independent with Fulbert Youlou as president.

title: Trois Glorieuses
description: Three days of strikes and crowds force the unpopular President Youlou out, bringing in the left-leaning Massamba-Débat.

title: Ngouabi takes power
description: Captain Marien Ngouabi's National Revolutionary Movement unseats Massamba-Débat after months of militia street fighting.

title: People's Republic proclaimed
description: Congo declares itself the first Marxist-Leninist state in Africa and remodels its flag, anthem and economy on the East.

title: Ngouabi assassinated
description: Commandos shoot the president in a plot never solved; Massamba-Débat is executed for it and Yhombi-Opango takes over.

title: Sassou Nguesso becomes president
description: Denis Sassou Nguesso, 36, wins the party contest to rule, beginning an ascendancy that lasts, with one break, for forty years.

title: Lissouba elected
description: Multiparty elections make Pascal Lissouba president; Sassou's party retains the army's loyalty and its militia, the Cobras, wait.

title: First civil war
description: Disputed elections send rival party militias into Brazzaville's southern districts, killing thousands before a truce.

title: Civil war brings Sassou back
description: Five months of artillery war end with Sassou's Cobras, backed by Angolan armour, taking the capital and the presidency.

title: Peace accords end the war
description: The government and rebel militias sign ceasefire agreements at Pointe-Noire, though unrest smoulders in the Pool region.

title: Sassou re-elected
description: With the opposition boycotting, Sassou Nguesso wins another seven-year term amid fraud claims.

title: Referendum scraps term limits
description: A new constitution removes the age and term barriers, and Sassou wins a fifth decade in power at the following election.
